description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotional categories in a dataset of emotional speech, with each slice representing a distinct emotion and its corresponding proportion. The chart is divided into six labeled segments: "Frustration" (25.1%, light blue), "Neutral" (23.1%, dark blue), "Happiness" (8.1%, light blue), "Excitement" (14.1%, red), "Sadness" (approximately 10%, orange), and "Anger" (14.9%, yellow). Each segment is clearly labeled with its emotional category and percentage value, and the slices are arranged in a clockwise sequence starting from the top. The visual representation emphasizes the relative frequency of each emotion, with "Frustration" being the largest category, followed by "Neutral," while "Happiness" accounts for the smallest proportion. The chart does not include a legend, as all labels are directly placed within or adjacent to the slices, and no slices are visually separated or emphasized beyond their size and color.
